thread:
jia: quick update from the bisect — nailed down the regression to the int4 packer reorder change (commit ab12f3 -> introduced head-major->head-minor swap). detailed notes below.
jia: TL;DR: token id collisions on em-dash clusters were caused by a byte-ordering mismatch in the packer header that made our tokenizer overlay map into a different id range for some multi-byte tokens when run through the new packer. reverting the packer restores gold logits.
jia: small repro I used:
```
# build candidate with old/new packer knobs
./build.sh --quant-packer=head-major  # old (gold)
./build.sh --quant-packer=head-minor  # new (regression)
python -m evals.sanity --model mistralx:int4 --prompts tests/punct-heavy.txt --dump-token-ids out/ids.json
```
jia: sample failing diff:
- gold token ids: [5023, 19, 88, 9999, 5]
- head-minor run:   [5023, 19, 88, 9987, 5]  <-- clash at 4th id only with head-minor packer
- head-major run:   [5023, 19, 88, 9999, 5]  (matches gold)
vikram: good catch. do we know whether this is purely input-token remap (tokenizer overlay) or an internal uint packing interpretation?
jia: dug into the packer header bytes. the new packer writes per-head bitoffsets in little-endian while our tokenizer overlay loader expects big-endian offsets for multi-byte token encodings. result: some multichar sequences map to the wrong index range.
lucas: so two things colliding: tokenizer overlay format assumption + packer endian switch. explains why Gemma (which has a different overlay loader variant) didn't hit it.
mika: can we patch a tiny shim to normalize header endianness at load time? that would be faster than rolling back packer in prod.
jia: I prototyped a shim in the runtime: load_header(); if magic==0x4d52 then byte-swap offsets; else keep. quick test: shim applied -> token ids align, ppl back to baseline within noise (12.1 vs 12.0).
lucas: nice. but we should still fix packer to be explicit about endianness and add a serialization version tag.
vikram: also run the rotary_scale toggle to confirm no remaining kv-warmup amplification. did that already?
jia: yes — ran rotary_scale=1.0 and rotary_autotune=off on the head-minor build with shim: early warmup logit transients reduced but there's still a ~0.2 ppl delta on the first 6 tokens vs gold. likely residual head-indexing variance in int4 kernels.
lucas: I'll push a kernel sanity patch that enforces head-major addressing when decoding kv offsets; if that reduces the early-step delta we can keep shim short-lived. I'll run on the dedicated canary node.
mika: provisioning canary now. canary job:
- run 50-prompt repro (punct + emoji + sentinel)
- collect first-12-token decode traces per-head
- compare ppl and token id diffs
command: 
```
./ci/run_canary.sh --image=mx-int4-shim --prompts=tests/50-punct.txt --trace=first12 --out=artifacts/1769829999
```
triage-bot: created regression ticket RG-1769829999 and attached ci job 1769830400.
jia: artifacts uploaded: link to artifact bundle (logs/token-diffs/trace.json) on s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/1769829999.tar.gz
vikram: lucas, after your kernel patch, please run:
- old packer (head-major) baseline
- new packer (head-minor) without shim
- new packer with shim
collect ppl, token-diff rate, and early-token logit RMS per-head.
lucas: will do. expecting kernel address fix to remove the 0.2 ppl early bias. if not, we escalate to quant-engine and ABI folks.
mika: ops note: hold Hosted API canaries on MistralX int4 until we confirm either rollback or shim + kernel patch. tagging #eng-runtime.
jia: opened a small PR with the shim (rfc, tests) and the eval harness for cross-tokenizer checks: PR #8342.
vikram: thanks. next steps: 1) lucas pushes kernel patch + canary run 2) if green, remove shim and add serialization version tests 3) if not green, rollback packer change and coordinate with quant-engine for a proper packer spec.
mika: I'll keep the canary running and post updates to the ticket. ping me if you need longer retention on traces.
triage-bot: status: investigating -> mitigation-in-flight (shim) -> assigned to lucas.
jia: appreciate the quick loop. will follow up with a short postmortem once we close the RG ticket. :rocket:
